# scrin - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scrin/0.1.83/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/scrin/index.html

## Expand description

Scrin is a Rust terminal UI toolkit for building polished command-line interfaces without depending on Ratatui.

It provides a Scrin-native rendering model with buffers, colors, rectangles,
layout constraints, styled text, widgets, interaction metadata, panes,
overlays, command palettes, status bars, input routing, terminal lifecycle
helpers, and animation glue.
The effects layer is powered by [ aisling](https://crates.io/crates/aisling)
and adapts Aisling frames into Scrin buffers, so loaders and text effects can
be composed with normal Scrin widgets.

[§](https://docs.rs#install)Install

```
[dependencies]
scrin = "0.1.83"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#draw-a-widget)Draw A Widget

```
use scrin::core::buffer::Buffer;
use scrin::core::color::Color;
use scrin::core::rect::Rect;
use scrin::style::Style;
use scrin::widgets::block::Block;
use scrin::widgets::Widget;
let mut buffer = Buffer::new(40, 8);
buffer.fill(Rect::new(0, 0, 40, 8), ' ', Color::WHITE, None);
let block = Block::bordered()
    .title("scrin")
    .border_style(Style::new().fg(Color::CYAN));
block.render(&mut buffer, Rect::new(0, 0, 40, 8));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#render-an-aisling-effect-into-a-scrin-buffer)Render An Aisling Effect Into A Scrin Buffer

```
use scrin::core::{buffer::Buffer, rect::Rect};
use scrin::effects::{EffectKind, EffectPlayer};
let mut buffer = Buffer::new(60, 6);
let mut effect = EffectPlayer::new(EffectKind::Matrix, "Scrin + Aisling")
    .with_size(60, 6)
    .with_duration(24);
effect.render_to_buffer(&mut buffer, Rect::new(0, 0, 60, 6));
effect.advance();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#render-an-aisling-loader)Render An Aisling Loader

```
use scrin::core::{buffer::Buffer, rect::Rect};
use scrin::effects::{LoaderKind, LoaderPlayer};
let mut buffer = Buffer::new(48, 4);
let loader = LoaderPlayer::new(LoaderKind::Bar)
    .with_size(48, 4)
    .with_label("indexing".to_string());
let progress = LoaderPlayer::progress_from_fraction(0.42);
loader.render(3, progress, &mut buffer, Rect::new(0, 0, 48, 4));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#terminal-rendering)Terminal Rendering

[ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) uses Scrin’s diff presenter and updates only changed
cells.

[is available when an application wants a full buffer repaint every frame, for example during dense animation.](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw_full)

`Terminal::draw_full`[§](https://docs.rs#re-exports)Re-Exports

Common Aisling selector/config types are re-exported from [ effects](https://docs.rs/effects/index.html) so a
Scrin application can choose effects and loaders through one crate path.

[§](https://docs.rs#performance-apis)Performance APIs

Larger Scrin applications can use [ widgets::ScrollableText](https://docs.rs/widgets/scroll_text/struct.ScrollableText.html) for retained
styled-text wrapping,

[for cached Markdown rows, retained Aisling widgets through](https://docs.rs/widgets/markdown_output/struct.RetainedMarkdownOutput.html)

`widgets::RetainedMarkdownOutput`[and](https://docs.rs/effects/retained/struct.RetainedEffectWidget.html)

`effects::RetainedEffectWidget`[, dirty-rectangle presentation through](https://docs.rs/effects/retained/struct.RetainedLoaderWidget.html)

`effects::RetainedLoaderWidget`[, strategy-based drawing through](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.Terminal.html#method.present_areas)

`Terminal::present_areas`[, cursor-preserving area draws through](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw_with_present_strategy)

`Terminal::draw_with_present_strategy`[, frame diagnostics through](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw_area_preserve_cursor_timed)

`Terminal::draw_area_preserve_cursor_timed`[/](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.FrameTiming.html)

`FrameTiming`[/](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.FrameDiagnostic.html)

`FrameDiagnostic`[, and shared widget roles through](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.NamedFrameTiming.html)

`NamedFrameTiming`[. Retained Aisling hot paths can use](https://docs.rs/theme/struct.ThemeTokens.html)

`ThemeTokens`[and](https://docs.rs/effects/retained/struct.RetainedEffectWidget.html#method.render_frame_into)

`effects::RetainedEffectWidget::render_frame_into`[to avoid mutating widget state or doing unexpected cache rebuild work.](https://docs.rs/effects/retained/struct.RetainedEffectWidget.html#method.render_cached_only)

`effects::RetainedEffectWidget::render_cached_only`[§](https://docs.rs#interaction-apis)Interaction APIs

[ interaction](https://docs.rs/interaction/index.html) contains stable

[values,](https://docs.rs/interaction/struct.WidgetId.html)

`WidgetId`[metadata,](https://docs.rs/interaction/struct.HitRegion.html)

`HitRegion`[roles, selectable spans, hover tracking, selection models, and normalized](https://docs.rs/interaction/enum.WidgetRole.html)

`WidgetRole`[output for mouse move/down/drag/up/click events. Frames can register metadata with](https://docs.rs/interaction/enum.UiEvent.html)

`UiEvent`[,](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.Frame.html#method.register_hit_region)

`Frame::register_hit_region`[, and](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.Frame.html#method.register_selectable_span)

`Frame::register_selectable_span`[. Terminals can query the latest frame with](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.Frame.html#method.mark_dirty)

`Frame::mark_dirty`[,](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.Terminal.html#method.hit_test)

`Terminal::hit_test`[,](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.Terminal.html#method.scroll_hit_test)

`Terminal::scroll_hit_test`[, and](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.Terminal.html#method.selectable_at)

`Terminal::selectable_at`[.](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.Terminal.html#method.handle_pointer_event)

`Terminal::handle_pointer_event`Metadata-aware widget surfaces include [ widgets::CodeBlock](https://docs.rs/widgets/code/struct.CodeBlock.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/widgets/markdown_output/struct.RetainedMarkdownOutput.html)

`widgets::RetainedMarkdownOutput`[,](https://docs.rs/widgets/scroll_text/struct.ScrollableText.html)

`widgets::ScrollableText`[,](https://docs.rs/widgets/list/struct.List.html)

`widgets::List`[,](https://docs.rs/widgets/tabs/struct.Tabs.html)

`widgets::Tabs`[,](https://docs.rs/widgets/transcript_viewport/struct.TranscriptViewport.html)

`widgets::TranscriptViewport`[,](https://docs.rs/widgets/status_deck/struct.StatusDeck.html)

`widgets::StatusDeck`[,](https://docs.rs/widgets/todo_list/struct.TodoList.html)

`widgets::TodoList`[,](https://docs.rs/widgets/pane_cockpit/struct.PaneCockpit.html)

`widgets::PaneCockpit`[, and](https://docs.rs/widgets/kanban_board/struct.KanbanBoard.html)

`widgets::KanbanBoard`[.](https://docs.rs/effects/retained/struct.CachedEffectPane.html)

`effects::CachedEffectPane`[§](https://docs.rs#application-validation)Application Validation

Full-screen applications should pair Scrin’s crate-level tests with app-level pseudo-terminal captures for frame output, prompt input, overlays, provider setup, and terminal restore paths. A real-terminal visual pass is still useful for subjective clipping, spacing, contrast, and animation pacing.

# Aisling in scrin_widgets - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scrin-widgets/0.2.6/scrin_widgets/struct.Aisling.html

# Struct Aisling

[Source](../src/scrin_widgets/lib.rs.html#339-342) `pub struct Aisling<W> {  }`

## Expand description

Wraps any Scrin widget with an Aisling post-render effect.

Creates an effect wrapper around any Scrin widget.

Replaces the effect used by the wrapper.

Sets effect strength on a 0..=10 scale.

Performs copy-assignment from

`source`.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html#method.clone_from)

Formats the value using the given formatter.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Debug.html#tymethod.fmt)

Tests for `self` and `other` values to be equal, and is used by `==`.

Tests for `!=`. The default implementation is almost always sufficient,
and should not be overridden without very good reason.

Decorates this widget with the default Aisling effect.

Immutably borrows from an owned value.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/borrow/trait.Borrow.html#tymethod.borrow)

Mutably borrows from an owned value.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/borrow/trait.BorrowMut.html#tymethod.borrow_mut)

🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (`clone_to_uninit`)

Performs copy-assignment from

`self` to

`dest`.

[Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.CloneToUninit.html#tymethod.clone_to_uninit)

Returns the argument unchanged.

Calls `U::from(self)`.

That is, this conversion is whatever the implementation of
[From](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)<T> for U

The resulting type after obtaining ownership.

Creates owned data from borrowed data, usually by cloning.

`pub struct SplitPane { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Computes two sub-areas from a parent area with a ratio and optional divider.

The ratio controls how much space the first pane gets (0.0..1.0). The divider is rendered between the two panes and takes 1 cell.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# StreamPanel in scrin_widgets - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scrin-widgets/0.2.6/scrin_widgets/struct.StreamPanel.html

`pub struct StreamPanel<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A streaming log or code output panel with auto-scroll and optional line numbers.

Feed it lines via `.lines()` and control the scroll with `.scroll_offset()`.
When `follow_tail` is true (default), new lines auto-scroll to the bottom.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# yatrosci-ode 0.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/yatrosci-ode/0.1.0

Numerical integration of ordinary differential equations, providing
functionality equivalent to `scipy.integrate`.

## Overview

This crate provides:

- Initial value problem (IVP) solvers
- Explicit methods (Euler, RK4, RK45/Dormand-Prince)
- Implicit methods for stiff problems (Implicit Euler, BDF)
- Adaptive step size control
- Dense output interpolation

## Example

```
use ;
use array;
// Define the ODE: dy/dt = -y (exponential decay)
let f = ;
let y0 = array!;
let t_span = ;
let result = solve_ivp.unwrap;
```

# ndarray - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ndarray/^0.16/

## Expand description

The `ndarray` crate provides an *n*-dimensional container for general elements
and for numerics.

In *n*-dimensional we include, for example, 1-dimensional rows or columns,
2-dimensional matrices, and higher dimensional arrays. If the array has *n*
dimensions, then an element in the array is accessed by using that many indices.
Each dimension is also called an *axis*.

- `ArrayBase`- *n*-dimensional array type itself.
 It is used to implement both the owned arrays and the views; see its docs for an overview of all array features.
- The main specific array type is `Array`

[§](https://docs.rs#highlights)Highlights

- Generic *n*-dimensional array
- [Slicing](https://docs.rs/struct.ArrayBase.html#slicing), also with arbitrary step size, and negative indices to mean elements from the end of the axis.
- Views and subviews of arrays; iterators that yield subviews.
- Higher order operations and arithmetic are performant
- Array views can be used to slice and mutate any `[T]`data using`ArrayView::from`and`ArrayViewMut::from`.
- `Zip`- `NdProducer`

[§](https://docs.rs#crate-status)Crate Status

-
Still iterating on and evolving the crate - The crate is continuously developing, and breaking changes are expected during evolution from version to version. We adopt the newest stable rust features if we need them.
- Note that functions/methods/traits/etc. hidden from the docs are not considered part of the public API, so changes to them are not considered breaking changes.

-
Performance: - Prefer higher order methods and arithmetic operations on arrays first, then iteration, and as a last priority using indexed algorithms.
- The higher order functions like `.map()``.map_inplace()``.zip_mut_with()``Zip``azip!()`
- Performance of an operation depends on the memory layout of the array or array view. Especially if it’s a binary operation, which needs matching memory layout to be efficient (with some exceptions).
- Efficient floating point matrix multiplication even for very large matrices; can optionally use BLAS to improve it further.

-
**MSRV: Requires Rust 1.64 or later**

[§](https://docs.rs#crate-feature-flags)Crate Feature Flags

The following crate feature flags are available. They are configured in your
`Cargo.toml`. See [ doc::crate_feature_flags](https://docs.rs/doc/crate_feature_flags/index.html) for more information.

- `std`: Rust standard library-using functionality (enabled by default)
- `serde`: serialization support for serde 1.x
- `rayon`: Parallel iterators, parallelized methods, the- `parallel`- `par_azip!`
- `approx`Implementations of traits from the- `approx`
- `blas`: transparent BLAS support for matrix multiplication, needs configuration.
- `matrixmultiply-threading`: Use threading from- `matrixmultiply`.

[§](https://docs.rs#documentation)Documentation

-
The docs for `ArrayBase`*n*-dimensional array type. Other good pages to look at are the documentation for the`s![]``azip!()`
-
If you have experience with NumPy, you may also be interested in `ndarray_for_numpy_users`

[§](https://docs.rs#the-ndarray-ecosystem)The ndarray ecosystem

`ndarray` provides a lot of functionality, but it’s not a one-stop solution.

`ndarray` includes matrix multiplication and other binary/unary operations out of the box.
More advanced linear algebra routines (e.g. SVD decomposition or eigenvalue computation)
can be found in [ ndarray-linalg](https://crates.io/crates/ndarray-linalg).

The same holds for statistics: `ndarray` provides some basic functionalities (e.g. `mean`)
but more advanced routines can be found in [ ndarray-stats](https://crates.io/crates/ndarray-stats).

If you are looking to generate random arrays instead, check out [ ndarray-rand](https://crates.io/crates/ndarray-rand).

For conversion between `ndarray`, [ nalgebra](https://crates.io/crates/nalgebra) and

[check out](https://crates.io/crates/image)

`image`[.](https://crates.io/crates/nshare)

`nshare`## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- Producers, iterables and iterators.
- [linalg](https://docs.rs/linalg/index.html)
